messages:
Maya (Support): FYI escalation from Acme Corp — they report a sharp spike where streaming requests that the client aborted are showing up as 5xx in our metrics and they were billed for the tokens that were still in-flight. Customer supplied logs and a tiny repro. Can we triage?

Jon (Platform): ack. Can you paste the exact repro they ran? curious if this is chunked encoding + early FIN or a proxy race.

Maya (Support): pasted what they gave:
```
# client: node streaming abort
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"small-m","input":"long stream..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate &
sleep 1; kill $!   # client kills connection while stream still in progress
```
Server logs from customer side show ECONNRESET after some chunks. They expect the call to be counted as client-abort/no-charge, but our dashboard shows a 502 and token billing for the partial stream.

Priya (SRE): saw a handful of similar reports last week. Quick hypothesis: gateway treats an unexpected proxy EOF (no final chunk/trailer) as a backend failure and marks request as 5xx. We then propagate that status into billing. Need to classify mid-stream client disconnects differently.

Jon (Platform): digging into gateway logs, grep I used:
```
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/gateway -c proxy | grep "chunked.*unexpected EOF\|broken pipe\|client reset"
```
Example lines we see in staging (trimmed):
```
2026-02-21T14:12:02Z proxy: stream_id=abc123 client=1.2.3.4 chunked: unexpected EOF before final chunk
2026-02-21T14:12:02Z proxy: stream_id=abc123 upstream: write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->10.0.1.9:42312: broken pipe
```
Current heuristic: if proxy returns an error before seeing upstream response trailer we set status=502. That lumps client-aborts (RST/FIN) with real upstream 5xx.

Maya (Support): customer attached billing snapshot showing tokens billed at 0:00-01:00 window matching those lines. They want a credit if this is our misclassification.

Alex (Billing): we can do a one-off credit but we need a reproducible signal to detect "client-abort" vs actual gateway errors. Please add clear fingerprints in the runbook so we can automate credits for similar cases.

Priya (SRE): proposed short triage/runbook:
1) Reproduce locally using the customer's script or `socat`/`nc` to half-close:
```
# send a partial chunk and close connection
printf "POST /v1/streams/generate HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.example\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nAuthorization: Bearer $KEY\r\n\r\n5\r\nhello\r\n" | nc api.redwood.example 443; # then close socket
```
2) Capture gateway logs at the time (grep patterns above) and note if we see `unexpected EOF` + `broken pipe` with no upstream 5xx body.
3) Correlate with routing trace: traceroute id in proxy logs -> identify if upstream model-worker returned any status before EOF. If no upstream status, mark as client_abort candidate.
4) For billing: flag requests where (a) connection closed by client (RST/FIN), (b) no upstream error code or body, and (c) token stream incomplete -> classify as `client_aborted_stream` and do not bill tokens beyond last ACKed chunk.
```
Note: step 3 requires we have trace IDs on each chunk; we do in dedicated-prod via header X-Trace-Id.

Jon (Platform): technical note — IPv6 NAT clients sometimes send FIN then more data arrives from intermediate proxies causing `write: broken pipe` on our side. That still should be a client-side abort. I will open a small change to the gateway logic (PR-plat-918) to:
- differentiate syscall errors: if cause is `write: broken pipe` or `read: connection reset by peer` and no upstream status, set internal classification `client_abort` instead of 502.
- emit metric `stream.client_abort` with labels (route, model, customer_id)
This will let billing decide to exclude those from 5xx counts.

CI-Bot: CI run for PR-plat-918 queued. All integration tests run in ~12m.

Priya (SRE): short-term mitigation: we can add a rule in the billing pipeline to ignore requests that match the log fingerprint (proxy: chunked unexpected EOF + broken pipe and trace missing upstream status) for credits. I'll need a grepable signature and a sample window to confirm false positives.

Alex (Billing): please create a support ticket SUP-4521 and include the predicate. For this specific customer we can issue a manual credit once SRE confirms fingerprint.

Maya (Support): created SUP-4521 and attached customer logs + our staging repro. Customer confirms they can reproduce reliably with the Node snippet.

Jon (Platform): follow-ups:
- I'll push PR-plat-918 to staging tomorrow and add the `stream.client_abort` metric.
- Add an end-to-end test that simulates client half-close and asserts we do NOT count it as 5xx.

Priya (SRE): once metric exists I'll run a 48h scan to find historical occurrences and give a list of affected customers for billing.

Alex (Billing): agreed — hold off mass credits until we have the metric and a clear list. We'll do manual for Acme in the meantime.

Maya (Support): will update customer: we have a triage & short-term credit plan, longer-term fix in progress (gateway heuristics + metric). Thanks team :thumbsup:

Jon (Platform): quick note on customer mitigation in their code: recommend they send a `Connection: close` header before killing the client process so the gateway can see intent; not ideal but reduces races. Also set `Expect: 100-continue` not required here but helps some proxies.

Priya (SRE): marking this P1 for SRE/Platform until metric/PR are merged. I opened incident INC-2026-11 to track progress.

Alex (Billing): processed manual credit for Acme under SUP-4521.

Maya (Support): closing loop with customer, they confirmed credit received and traffic looks good. Will reopen if they see new anomalies.

Jon (Platform): tagging folks: @Priya @Alex @Maya — I'll post PR link once CI passes.

CI-Bot: PR-plat-918 merged to staging (CI green).
